newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish board may ease disclosure rule.
newsitem.headline: Turkish board may ease disclosure rule.

text.p: Turkish Capital Markets Board (SPK) chairman Ali Ihsan Karacan said on Thursday a new rule requiring all foreign investors on the Istanbul Stock Exchange to disclose their identity may be eased conditionally.

Under the new rule, all brokers and banks have to ask details of the identity of investing foreign institutions and individuals and report them to the Board in order to be able to carry out clients' buy or sell orders.

The SPK began enforcing the rule last week following the refusal by foreign institutions to disclose their clients' names when requested to do so by the SPK during investigations in August into the alleged manipulation of shares in Turkish Airlines.
Karacan told reporters on Thursday that client information was not needed on a daily basis.

However, under the new proposal it must be "supplied when we want to carry out an investigation...Our condition for easing this rule is to get a written guarantee from everyone who will make (share) deals in Turkey that he will definitely disclose information when requested," he said.
Karacan defended the rule as the SPK's right as a local regulatory body and dismissed criticisms that it would discourage foreign capital influx.
